s5.label: Sonnet 5
s5.note: the published Sonnet 5 arm, whole corpus

reader_level.label: viewed a crop
looked at its answer drawn back
diffed render against source in code
ran OSRA

typical: Opens the first image and works it to an answer before opening the next (91% of ten-image readers).
Sets up: installs RDKit or a venv itself (28%); lays a pixel grid over the drawing to read coordinates (43%).
Small drawings (under 25 heavy atoms) take a median 5 tool calls each; from 45 atoms up, 25, with 11.7 crops viewed per image against 1.7 on small ones.
Checks the SMILES with RDKit (98% of readers) and draws it back on 61% of images, looking at the render on 60%.
OSRA is a side check at most: 7% of readers ran it, as often on one image as over all of them.
Writes the answers file at the end (97% of readers first write it in the last fifth of their steps). About 4 min 40 s, 24k output tokens and $0.92 per image at list price.

method: Every tool call in every scored reader's transcript, classified by what it did. A command that crops and renders counts once in the mix (render wins) but sets both flags.
A call belongs to an image when it names exactly one blind image or a file named after one; a call naming none inherits the image the reader was last on. Calls naming several images are batch-level.
Thinking is redacted in transcripts, so output tokens (which include it) stand in for it.
Correlation, not causation: harder drawings attract more cropping and more checking, so every technique-vs-accuracy figure is split by drawing size.

The two models had different prompts. The Sonnet 5.5 prompt names cropping with PIL and an RDKit parse check; it does not ask for the answer to be drawn back. Most Sonnet 5 prompts did ask for a re-render.
